notes: All 5 without-skill assertion failures are skill-added structure (role transcript, proposal-written-to-file, explicit decision-handoff to user). Content assertions do not discriminate: baselines found every seeded flaw in all 3 evals.
The explicit 'user decides' handoff is the most discriminating guarantee: 2 of 3 baselines ended with a verdict instead of handing the decision back.

Token cost is 2-4x with skill (108k-186k vs 25k-82k per eval), and with-skill numbers are lower bounds: all 3 runs hit orchestration stalls plus a session-limit reset, so timing comparisons this iteration are not clean.
Prompt phrasing leaks structure: 'run a debate review' pushed 2 of 3 baselines to improvise their own multi-round adversarial format unprompted, shrinking the observable delta.

Fabrication risk found in with-skill pytest run: roles invented project facts (30-min CI, 4 shards, team experience ratios) and built quantitative rulings on them; no assertion polices factual grounding.
Orchestration defect in the skill: all 3 with-skill orchestrators spawned their first role subagent in the background and stalled waiting; SKILL.md never says to run phases synchronously.
Role-brief defect: role subagents tried to SendMessage a parent named 'general-purpose' instead of returning their one-line confirmation as final text.

Graders flagged assertion-wording issues: 'compromise proposed' is ambiguous when a report says 'zero compromises were needed' (inter-role bargaining vs design mitigations), and structure assertions test section presence, not genuine role independence.
